ingredient_lines.original_text: ¼ cup cornstarch or rice flour

steps: Put the sugar, coconut milk, coconut cream and salt in a saucepan. Heat until the sugar dissolves and the milk begins to simmer.
Meanwhile, mix 3 tablespoons or more of the cold cream into the cornflour and whisk to a smooth, thick paste with no lumps.
When the milk simmers, add the rest of the cream and the cornflour paste.
Keep the heat low and stir constantly until the pudding thickens. Stir in the orange blossom water, if using.
Pour into small bowls or pudding moulds.
Chill in the fridge for 2 hours.
To serve, turn each pudding out onto a plate and sprinkle with cinnamon.

recipes.title: Cantonese crispy fried chicken
recipes.description: A Hong Kong banquet favourite: a whole chicken poached with five-spice, glazed, dried, then deep-fried until the skin is glassy and crisp, with Sichuan pepper salt.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.note: or enough for your deep-fat fryer
lines.original_text: 4 cups oil (or enough for deep fryer)
Prawn crackers/shrimp chips (not the ready made ones)

steps: For the pepper salt, put the salt and Sichuan peppercorns in a small frying pan over a medium-low heat until they barely smoke. Take off the heat.
Grind them well with a pestle and mortar, or with a rolling pin, then mix in the MSG.
Clean and rinse the chicken, discarding the giblets. This and the next five steps can be done the day before, keeping the chicken in the fridge.
Bring enough water to cover the chicken to the boil in a large pot. Tie the five-spice, ginger and spring onions in a piece of muslin, add them to the water and simmer for 15 minutes.

Add the chicken, turn the heat down and poach it gently for 20 minutes. Poaching is gentler than simmering, at about 70–80°C: boiled, the meat turns tough and dry, and the lower the heat, the longer it takes.
Lift out the chicken, pat it dry with kitchen paper and leave it to air-dry for a little while. A dry skin helps the syrup stick.
Heat the vinegar and sugar in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves, to make a syrup.
Coat the chicken all over, inside and out, with the syrup, then leave it in a breeze until very dry. This second drying is what makes the skin crisp.

Heat the oil in a deep-fat fryer to 175°C. Too cool, and the sugar won't caramelise or brown the skin; too hot, and it burns. Without a thermostat, use a frying thermometer. If you fry in a wok or pan on the hob instead, take great care: it can tip and spill hot oil, which burns badly and can catch fire.
Deep-fry the chicken for about 10 minutes on each side, until brown and cooked through, 75°C in the thickest part.
Lift it out of the oil and chop it with a cleaver into pieces about 3 × 5 cm.
Fry the prawn crackers in the hot oil and sprinkle them with a little salt.
Serve the chicken surrounded by the prawn crackers, with the pepper salt in a small dish on the side.

recipes.title: Steamed pork with mustard greens
recipes.description: A quick Hakka-style stir-fry: thin slices of marinated pork tenderloin tossed with black bean sauce and blanched mustard greens.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 tsp cornstarch combined with 1 tsp cold water
1 tsp cornstarch combined with 1 tsp cold water
2 tbsp black bean and garlic sauce

steps: Wash the greens and discard the tough stems.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil, add the greens and cook for 2 minutes.
Drain the greens and rinse them under cold water to stop them cooking. Drain again, then cut them into long diagonal strips.

In a medium bowl, mix the cornflour and cold water, then stir in the sugar, soy sauce and rice wine. Slice the pork thinly, add it to the bowl and leave to marinate for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Heat the oil in a hot wok or large heavy frying pan over a medium heat. Add the black bean sauce and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the mustard greens and the 2 tbsp of water. Mix well and simmer gently for 4–5 minutes, until the pork is cooked through and the greens are tender.
Season with pepper and serve.

recipes.title: Bouillabaisse
recipes.description: Marseille's fish stew: several kinds of whole fish simmered with tomatoes, fennel and saffron, the broth poured over bread spread with garlicky rouille.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 660 g whole cleaned lotte, or monkfish
1 live octopus (optional), cleaned and cut into pieces

lines.note: peeled and cut into large slices
lines.original_text: 1 kg of potatoes, peeled and cut into large slices
5 ripe tomatoes, peeled, quartered and without seeds

steps: Scale the fish and wash them, in sea water if you can. Cut them into large slices, leaving the bones in.
Warm the olive oil for the broth in a large, deep saucepan.
Add the onions, 6 of the garlic cloves, crushed, the octopus pieces, if using, and the tomatoes. Brown them over a low heat for 5 minutes, turning them gently.

Add the fish slices, the large ones first and then the smaller ones. Cover with boiling water and add salt, cayenne pepper, the fennel, the bouquet garni and the saffron. Simmer over a low heat, stirring from time to time so the fish doesn't stick to the pan, and adjust the seasoning. Take the pan off the heat once the oil and water have thoroughly blended with the other ingredients, after about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the rouille. Remove the green shoots from the 2 garlic cloves and crush them to a fine paste in a mortar. Add the egg yolk and the saffron, then work in the olive oil a little at a time with the pestle to make a mayonnaise. Season with salt and cayenne pepper.
Cook the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes. Open the sea urchins with a pair of scissors and scoop out the roe with a small spoon.
Stir the sea urchin roe into the broth.
Rub the slices of bread with the last garlic clove and spread a tablespoon of rouille on each. Put at least 2 slices in each serving bowl.
Lift the fish out of the broth and arrange it on a large serving platter with the drained potatoes.
Pour the hot broth into the bowls over the bread and rouille, and serve the fish and potatoes on the platter alongside.

recipes.title: Choucroute
recipes.description: Alsace's choucroute garnie: sauerkraut braised in white wine with juniper and spices, heaped with smoked pork, bacon, sausages and potatoes.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 or so tablespoons of duck fat
1 or so tablespoons of coriander seed

ingredient_lines.note: or the same amount of salted pork belly, cut into rough squares
ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 strips of bacon (or the same amount of salted pork belly), sliced into rough squares
1 cup (240 ml) or so of white wine (dry)

steps: In a pot large enough to hold everything in the end, melt the duck fat over a medium heat.
When it is hot, add the onion and fry until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut, white wine, juniper berries, clove, coriander seeds, mustard seeds and garlic.
Add the smoked pork and the bacon.
Cover and simmer for about 2 hours.
In another pan, simmer the peeled potatoes and the sausages. Don't let them boil, or the sausages will split open.
Simmer until the potatoes are done; by then the sausages will be too.
Serve in a heap: the sauerkraut at the bottom, with the pork, sausages and potatoes on top.

recipes.title: Lemon mille-feuille
recipes.description: Three crisp, sugar-glazed strips of puff pastry stacked with a sharp lemon custard between them.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Unroll the pastry on a lightly floured surface.
Trim the pastry to a rectangle of about 23 × 25.5 cm.
Roll the larger piece of pastry out to a 30 cm square, using a very even, gentle pressure on the rolling pin so the edges stay neat.
Grease a baking tray and use the rolling pin to lift the pastry onto it.
Prick the pastry all over with a fork and brush it with the beaten egg.
Bake on a high shelf for 12–15 minutes, until crisp and golden.
To make it extra crisp, heat the grill to its highest setting, sift 1 tsp of the icing sugar over the pastry and flash it under the grill.
Take it out from under the grill and cut the square into three equal strips with a sharp knife.
Turn the strips over, sift the rest of the icing sugar over them and flash them under the grill again.
Cool on a wire rack, then keep in an airtight box with greaseproof paper between the layers until needed.
For the filling, put the egg yolks and the whole egg into a roomy bowl.
Whisk them with the caster sugar using an electric mixer until pale, thick and creamy, 4–5 minutes, adding the milk as you mix.
Sift the flour over the mixture and whisk again until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a saucepan and cook over a medium heat, whisking all the time, until it boils and thickens, then cook for 1 minute more. Take it off the heat and leave to cool.
Stir in the lemon zest and juice.
Put a pastry strip on a plate and cover it with half the lemon filling.
Put the second pastry strip on top and cover it with the rest of the filling.
Finish with the last pastry strip.

recipes.title: Pot-au-feu
recipes.description: A rustic French one-pot of beef and winter vegetables cooked in a broth coloured with charred onion; the broth is served first, then the meat with mustard and horseradish.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 2 ea. (~600 g) turnips (each is one handful)
½ ea. (~400 g) celery root OR 3–4 celery stalks

lines.note: of thyme, bay leaf and parsley
lines.original_text: A bouquet garni made of thyme, bay leaf, and parsley
Nutmeg (if you plan to serve the broth as the first course, i.e. the traditional way)

lines.note: a cheaper, tougher cut such as chuck
lines.original_text: 1 kg low-cost, tougher beef meat (e.g. beef chuck)

steps: Push the cloves into the onions, so they are easy to take out after cooking.

Peel the onions and cut them in half. Line a frying pan with foil and char the cut faces of the onions on it until completely black. This gives the broth a slightly smoky taste and its golden brown colour.
While the onions char, peel the turnips, carrots and celeriac and cut them into large pieces.
Trim the roots off the leeks, wash the green parts well and cut each leek into 2 or 3 pieces. The tougher green part goes in too.
Leave the quarter of cabbage in one piece.

Put all the vegetables, the ground pepper and the bouquet garni into a pressure cooker, packing them in as tightly as you can. Add enough water to cover the vegetables, but never fill a pressure cooker more than two-thirds to three-quarters full (check its instructions). If you can't cover the vegetables, add as much water as you can.
Add salt and cook the vegetables under pressure for 20 minutes.
Cool the pressure cooker under cold running water so you can open it, then lift out the vegetables and keep them to one side. Throw away the onions and the bouquet garni.
You should now have a golden brown broth. Taste it and add more salt or pepper if needed; it won't have its final flavour until the meat has cooked in it.
Put the meat into the broth and cook under pressure for 60–75 minutes.
If you are using marrowbones, cook them separately, or add them to the pressure cooker with the meat for the last 5 minutes.
Cool the pressure cooker under cold water again and open it. Lift out the meat and put the vegetables back into the broth. Bring the broth to the boil to warm them through while you slice the meat.

Serve the broth first, with a little grated nutmeg and toasted French bread. If you used marrowbones, spread the marrow on toast for anyone who wants some. Then bring the meat and vegetables to the table with strong mustard, horseradish sauce and gherkins.

recipes.title: Tourte à la Lorraine
recipes.description: A Lorraine meat pie of pork and veal marinated in Riesling and herbs, baked under puff pastry, with a nutmeg-scented cream custard poured in to finish.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Mix the meat with the Riesling, salt, pepper, quatre épices, shallots, garlic, onion, parsley, bay leaves, thyme and cloves.
Cover and leave to marinate in the fridge for 48 hours.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Press the shortcrust pastry into a buttered and floured pie dish, or a cake tin lined with baking paper.
Spread the meat over the pastry, leaving a narrow border all round the edge. Cover it with the puff pastry, moistening the edges with a little water to seal them together.
Brush the top with some of the egg yolk and make a small chimney in the middle (a tube of card wrapped in foil works). Score a pattern on top with the tip of a small knife.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, beat the whole egg and the rest of the yolk with the cream, and season with grated nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Take the pie out of the oven and pour the cream mixture in through the chimney with a funnel. This is a bit delicate: add a little at a time, tilting the dish to spread it through the pie.
Return the pie to the oven for 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Stollen
recipes.description: The German Christmas loaf: a buttery yeasted dough packed with rum-soaked fruit, peel and almonds, folded, baked and dusted thickly with icing sugar.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: halved; the original uses maraschino cherries

ingredient_lines.original_text: Dark rum or brandy: 4 tbsp, 60 g
Plain flour (or all-purpose flour): 1 pound (454 g)
Butter, diced and softened: 3 oz (85 g)

steps: Put the raisins, currants, mixed peel and cherries in a bowl with the rum or brandy and leave them to soak for at least 1 hour.
In a small bowl, stir the yeast and 1 tsp of the sugar into the warm water. Leave it for 5 minutes for fresh yeast, or 15 minutes for dried.
Sprinkle 1½ tbsp of the flour over the fruit with the almonds and stir until the flour is completely absorbed.
Warm the milk in a small pan until lukewarm and stir in the rest of the sugar until it dissolves. Stir in the lemon zest.
Put all but 50 g of the flour into a large bowl with the salt. Pour in the yeast mixture and mix thoroughly.
Add the egg and the sweetened milk to the flour, then beat in the softened butter.
Mix everything into a dough, turn it out onto a floured surface and knead it, working in the rest of the flour, until it is no longer sticky.
Knead in the fruit and almonds a little at a time.
Clean the large bowl and brush the inside with 1 tbsp of the melted butter.
Brush the top of the dough with another 2 tbsp of the melted butter and put it in the bowl.
Cover with a clean cloth and leave for 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Knock back the dough and leave it to rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the dough into a 30 × 20 cm rectangle and brush it with more of the melted butter.
Fold two opposite sides of the rectangle towards the middle so they overlap slightly, and press the join gently to hold it in place.
Taper the ends of the loaf slightly and push the sides gently together to form a mound along the middle. The loaf should be about 9 cm wide and 35 cm long.
Put the loaf on a floured baking tray and brush it with the rest of the melted butter. Leave it in a warm place for an hour, or until doubled in size.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Bake the stollen for 45 minutes, or until brown and crusty.
Leave the stollen to cool, then sift the icing sugar over the top.

recipes.title: Cinnamon-braised chicken
recipes.description: Kotopoulo kapama from the island of Kythera: chicken browned with cinnamon and bay, then braised slowly in tomato and red wine and served over thin pasta with grated cheese.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: pieces, skin on and bone in, one per person

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 tin tomatoes, or 300 g of fresh tomatoes

ingredient_lines.note: stick, cut into thin 8 cm strips
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 stick of celery, cut into thin 3-inch strips

ingredient_lines.note: or other thin pasta, cooked, to serve
or another hard cheese, grated, to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and add the onions. Stir gently until they are well browned.

Add the chicken, bay leaves and cinnamon stick, and brown the chicken thoroughly on all sides, for at least 10 minutes. The aim is to draw as much flavour from the skin as possible, as it adds to the sauce later on.
Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, garlic, wine, ground cloves and a little water, and bring to the boil. Add the parsley, celery leaves, celery and carrot.
Add enough water to cover everything in the pot. Cook slowly over a low heat for at least 2 hours, so the sauce doesn't catch. Don't stir: it only breaks up the vegetables and chicken.
Serve with thin pasta, with plenty of grated cheese over the top.

recipes.title: Galaktoboureko
recipes.description: A Greek pastry of buttered filo layered around a vanilla semolina custard, baked golden and brushed with lemon syrup.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Mix the sugar, eggs and semolina in a saucepan. Stir in the milk, the vanilla pods and the salt, then the juice of the half lemon.
Bring the mixture to the boil, stirring with a fork the whole time. When it boils, turn the heat down low and keep stirring for another 10 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave to cool.
Brush each sheet of filo with melted butter.
Butter a baking tin and lay half the filo in it, sheet by sheet. Pour the cooled semolina custard over the pastry and cover it with the rest of the buttered filo.
Sprinkle the pastry with a little water.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 1 hour, then leave to cool.
For the syrup, put the water and sugar in a saucepan.
Bring to the boil and simmer for about 10 minutes.
Leave the syrup to cool.
Once it has cooled, stir in the lemon juice, so it keeps its fresh taste.
Brush the finished pastry with the syrup and serve.

recipes.title: Baingan bartha
recipes.description: A south Indian take on smoky mashed aubergine, charred over a flame and stirred through a fresh paste of coconut, green chilli and coriander.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Roast the aubergine directly over a low gas flame, turning it regularly, until the skin is blackened and brittle and the flesh soft, about 15–20 minutes.
Set it aside to cool.
Grind the chillies, coconut and coriander together in a food processor to a paste.
Peel the skin off the aubergine and mash the flesh by hand to an even pulp.
Mix in the coconut paste and the yoghurt or paneer, with salt to taste.
Serve with chapatis, dosa or rice.

recipes.title: Chicken vindaloo
recipes.description: A hot, vinegar-sharp curry from Goa: chicken cooked in a garlic and chilli spice paste, then simmered in a sauce of deeply browned, blended onions.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Pour enough vegetable oil into a heavy-based frying pan to cover the base, with a little extra, and heat it on the hob.
Slice the onions into fairly thin slivers. When the oil is very hot, add the onions.
Turn the heat down low so the onions fry gently. After about 3 minutes they should be starting to caramelise.
Gradually turn up the heat, stirring the onions all the time. You want them to brown well without burning.
Add the vinegar: it will sizzle, and after a while it will evaporate. Keep stirring and frying for several more minutes, until the onions are very brown but not burnt.
Lift the onions into a bowl, letting as much oil as possible drip back into the pan. You should have a bowl of nicely crisp fried onions.

Put the onions in a blender or food processor with about 1 tbsp of the oil and blend for about a minute to a fairly thick, dark brown sauce. This onion sauce gives the vindaloo most of its heat, which builds as you eat.
Scrape the sauce out of the blender and set it aside.
Roughly chop the garlic and ginger. Deseed the chillies and chop them the same way. Put the garlic, ginger and chillies in the food processor.
Blend until you have a fairly grainy but liquid paste. A small spice-grinder attachment wastes less.
Stir the turmeric, ground coriander, garam masala and cinnamon into the paste until well mixed, and set aside.
Lightly crush the peppercorns in a mortar and pestle. Once coarse, add the mustard seeds and rock salt and keep grinding until the spices form a coarse powder.
Pour a little oil into a saucepan and add the garlic and chilli paste and the ground pepper mix. The paste should sit in a little oil rather than touch the bottom of the pan.
When the paste is hot and bubbling, add the chicken. Keep stirring so the chicken takes up the spices, until it is browned and mostly cooked.

Add the onion sauce and stir for 1 minute. Add a little of the water and stir for another 2 minutes, then turn the heat down quite low. The sauce should be quite runny and orange-tan at this stage; a lot will evaporate as it cooks.
Now you can add vegetables, if you like: the frozen peas work well.
Cover the pan and cook for 30–40 minutes, checking and stirring every 5 or 10 minutes so it doesn't stick or burn. The sauce darkens as it cooks.
For the last 15 minutes of the cooking time, boil the rice in another pan.
Spoon the curry over the rice, scatter over the chopped coriander and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Gajjar halwa
recipes.description: Grated carrots simmered in milk with butter, cardamom, cashews and raisins until thick and sweet, a much-loved Indian pudding.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ cup (120 g) cashew nuts, broken

steps: Cut the blemished ends off the carrots, wash them and peel them.
Grate the carrots and put them in a saucepan.
Add the cashews, raisins, salt, sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, butter and milk.
Bring to the boil over the heat, stirring.
Cook until the milk has mostly evaporated.
Serve with a sprinkling of cinnamon on top.

recipes.title: Gulab jamun
recipes.description: Soft balls of milk powder dough, deep-fried until dark brown and left to soak overnight in a cardamom sugar syrup.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: A little over ¾ cup (200 ml) warm milk
2 ½ cups (600 ml) white granulated sugar

steps: Heat the oil 4–5 cm deep in a small saucepan over a medium heat.
Mix the milk powder, baking mix and melted butter in a metal bowl.

Slowly add the warm milk, 2 tbsp at a time, mixing it in with a wooden spoon to make a ball of dough. Keep adding milk until all the dry ingredients are taken up. The dough should be firm and moist but not sticky; if you add too much milk, work in a little more of the dry mixture, keeping to 3 parts milk powder to 1 part baking mix.
Roll the dough into evenly sized balls, so they cook at the same rate. The balls dry out quickly, so fry them within a few minutes.
Drop a few balls into the oil; don't crowd the pan, as they swell as they cook. They sink to the bottom, then float to the top. Stir regularly so they brown evenly.
When they are dark brown, lift them out of the oil and drain them on kitchen paper.
Repeat until all the dough is used up.
For the syrup, break the cardamom seeds out of their pods.
Separate the seeds and crush them to release their flavour.
Mix the water, sugar and cardamom and heat for 10 minutes. Don't overheat it, or the syrup will caramelise.
Soak the fritters in the syrup overnight.
Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Khara pongal
recipes.description: A savoury South Indian porridge of rice and moong dal, finished with ghee, black pepper, cumin, curry leaves and toasted cashews.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or butter, plus extra to taste

steps: Cook the rice and dal together in the water with the turmeric, in a pot or a pressure cooker, until mushy.
Heat a little of the ghee in a large pan and brown the cashew nuts. Lift them out of the pan.
Add the rest of the ghee and the oil to the pan and heat.
Add the spices, starting with the mustard seeds, then the cumin seeds, black pepper, green chillies and curry leaves, and finish with the cashew nuts.
Mix in the rice and dal and warm through. If it is too thick, add a little water.
Season with salt and more ghee to taste. You can also stir in some grated coconut at the end.

recipes.title: Sambar
recipes.description: A tangy South Indian stew of toor dal and vegetables with tamarind and sambar masala, finished with mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: cubed, such as tomato, potato, aubergine, drumsticks or okra
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 cup (240 ml) cubed mixed vegetables (see notes)
3 tbsp thickish tamarind pulp OR 1 tsp tamarind concentrate
1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves, to garnish

steps: Wash the dal and cook it in the water with the salt until completely tender and soft, with no whole grains left.
Add the sambar masala, sugar and vegetables, including the onion, and cook until the vegetables are tender. Then add the tamarind.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and add the mustard seeds. When they splutter, add the dried chillies and the curry leaves.
Stir 2 or 3 times, then add the dal mixture. Bring to the boil, then simmer for about 5 minutes.
Garnish with the coriander.

recipes.title: Ricotta lasagne
recipes.description: A big baked lasagne layered with a slow-simmered sausage and beef tomato sauce, herby ricotta, mozzarella and parmesan.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: tinned whole, undrained, halved and deseeded
ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 cups (1 kg / 2.2 lb) canned whole tomatoes, undrained, halved, seeds removed
16 oz (450 g) mozzarella cheese, thinly sliced (a wire cutter is nice for semi-soft cheeses like this)

steps: Remove the sausage skins and break the meat into small pieces.
In a large saucepan or casserole of about 5 litres, fry the sausage and beef mince with the onion and garlic over a medium heat until the meat is browned.
Add the sugar, 1 tbsp of salt, the basil, fennel seeds, pepper and half the parsley, and mix well.
Add the tomatoes, tomato purée and water, mashing the tomatoes a little. Bring the sauce to the boil, then turn down the heat, cover and simmer for 1½ hours, stirring now and then.
Heat the oven to 140°C (120°C fan).
Cook the lasagne sheets and drain them.
In a medium bowl, mix the ricotta, egg, ½ tsp of salt and the rest of the parsley.

Assemble the lasagne in a 33 × 23 × 5 cm roasting tin, from the bottom up: a layer of sauce (about 375 g); a layer of pasta, overlapping slightly; half the ricotta mixture; a third of the mozzarella; another layer of sauce (about 375 g); a sprinkling of parmesan, not quite covering the sauce; a layer of pasta; the rest of the ricotta mixture; another third of the mozzarella; the rest of the sauce; another sprinkling of parmesan; and the rest of the mozzarella.
Cover the lasagne with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake for 25 minutes more, or until bubbling and lightly browned. Leave to cool for at least 20 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Spaghetti with clams
recipes.description: Neapolitan spaghetti alle vongole: live clams steamed open with garlic, chilli and diced tomatoes, then tossed with the pasta and parsley.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: enough to cover the base of the pan

ingredient_lines.original_text: 225 g (8 oz) diced plum tomatoes (see notes)
225 g (8 oz) canned, shelled clams, thoroughly rinsed (optional)
Peperoncino or, less commonly, black pepper to taste

ingredient_lines.note: to taste, instead of the chilli
ingredient_lines.original_text: Peperoncino or, less commonly, black pepper to taste

steps: Bring the water to the boil in a large pot with 1 tbsp of salt.
Add the spaghetti once the water is boiling and cook until al dente, 7–8 minutes.
Pour enough olive oil into a large, wide pan to barely cover the base, and heat it.
Add the garlic and the chilli and fry until golden, about a minute. Take care not to burn the garlic.
Add the live clams and the tomatoes.
Cover the pan and cook for about 8 minutes, shaking it every minute or so to help the clams open. Throw away any that stay shut.
Drain the spaghetti and add it to the pan with the clams and tomatoes. Turn the heat down to low.
Add the tinned clams and the clam juice.
Season with salt (and black pepper, if you are not using the chilli) and toss until the pasta is well coated in the tomatoes and oil. Add another tablespoon of olive oil if you like.
Scatter over the parsley.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Struffoli
recipes.description: Neapolitan festive fritters: little balls of sherry-scented dough, deep-fried until golden and dipped in an orange and honey glaze.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.note: enough to make a soft dough

lines.original_text: Shortening or oil for deep frying

steps: Mix the eggs, oil, baking powder, cream of tartar, sugar and sherry. Work in enough flour to make a dough that is a little sticky but still workable.
Shape the dough into small balls about 1 cm across.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C to 190°C. Deep-fry the dough balls until golden brown and cooked through.
Stir the glaze ingredients together over a low heat until the sugar dissolves. Dip each fritter into the glaze and lift it out.

recipes.title: Grilled aubergine
recipes.description: Thick slices of aubergine grilled until tender, then spooned with a warm, sweet miso sauce and scattered with toasted sesame seeds.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Wash the aubergine and cut it lengthways into 2.5 cm slices.
Brush the cut sides with oil.
Grill 7–10 cm from the heat until the aubergine is tender and browned all over, about 5 minutes.
In a small saucepan, mix the miso, sugar and stock. Cook over a low heat, stirring, until smooth and hot. Don't let it boil.
Pour the sauce over the aubergine.
Toast the sesame seeds in a small frying pan until they start to jump, then sprinkle them over the aubergine.

recipes.title: Bizcochito
recipes.description: Crisp, crumbly anise biscuits from New Mexico, made with lard, cut into shapes and dusted with cinnamon sugar while still hot.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Cream the lard, sugar and aniseed in a large mixing bowl. Add the eggs and beat well.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt in another large bowl.
Add the flour to the creamed mixture a little at a time until a stiff dough forms.
Knead the dough lightly. Pat it out 0.5–1 cm thick, or roll it into a log 0.5–1 cm across.
Cut into shapes.
Bake in an oven heated to 180°C (160°C fan) for 10–12 minutes, or until golden brown.
Dust with the cinnamon sugar while still hot.
Leave to cool.

recipes.title: Chiles en nogada
recipes.description: Roasted poblano chillies stuffed with mince, fruit, almonds and raisins, fried in a light egg batter and covered in a creamy walnut sauce.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Cut the almonds into 2–4 pieces. Peel the peaches, apples and pears and chop them very finely. Set aside.
Fry the mince in a spoonful of oil in a frying pan over a low heat with garlic and salt to taste.
When the meat is cooked, add the fruit, almonds and raisins and fry for about 4 minutes. Leave to cool.
Toast the poblano chillies over a flame on the hob until charred.
Put the toasted chillies in water and slit each one down one long side. Wash away the veins and the dark charred spots.
Stuff the chillies with the fruit and meat mixture.
Separate the eggs. Whisk the whites until frothy, then beat in the flour and yolks until the batter turns pale yellow.
Dip each chilli in the batter and fry in a pan until light brown. Repeat until all the chillies are done, then set them aside while you make the nogada.
For the nogada, blend the walnuts, milk, cheese and rum for about a minute, until the sauce is white.
Pour the sauce over the chillies and serve.

recipes.title: Baklava
recipes.description: Layers of buttered filo and finely ground pistachios, cut into wedges, baked until crisp and soaked in a thick honey and vanilla syrup.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or walnuts, or any other nuts
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 lb (450 g) nuts (any type, but preferrably pistachios or walnuts)

steps: Put the nuts and cinnamon in a blender and blend them to a fine powder, taking care not to let it turn into a paste.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat, then set it aside.
Line a baking tin with baking parchment.
Count the sheets of filo pastry and divide the number by eight. Lay one-eighth of the sheets in the bottom of the tin, on the parchment.
Divide the ground nuts into seven equal portions.
Brush the filo with melted butter and scatter one portion of nuts evenly over it.
Lay another eighth of the filo sheets on top of the nuts.
Repeat the buttering and layering of nuts and filo until all the filo and nuts are used up.
With a sharp knife, cut the baklava into eight equal portions, cutting from the centre outwards like the lines of the Union Jack.
Bake for 25 minutes at 180°C (160°C fan). Take it out of the oven and leave it to cool slightly.

Mix the vanilla extract, honey, sugar and water in a clean saucepan. Boil over a medium heat until it becomes a very thick, viscous syrup of a little over 240 ml. Take it off the heat and leave it to cool slightly.
Pour the syrup over the baked baklava, coating each portion evenly. To avoid burns, wait until both the baklava and the syrup have cooled.
Leave everything to cool completely before serving.

recipes.title: Israeli salad
recipes.description: A crisp chopped salad of cucumber, tomato, onion and parsley in small even cubes, dressed with oil, lemon juice and za'atar.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 tsp za'atar (can substitute ¼ tsp thyme)

steps: Mix the cucumber, tomato, onion and parsley.
Mix the oil, lemon juice, salt, pepper and za'atar to make a dressing.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and adjust the seasoning to taste.

recipes.title: Kanafeh
recipes.description: Shredded kataifi pastry tossed in butter and layered around melting mozzarella and cream cheese, baked golden in a frying pan, then soaked in rose and orange blossom syrup and topped with walnuts.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Put the oven shelf in the lower middle of the oven and heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
In a medium bowl, mix the mozzarella and cream cheese, then set it aside.
Cut the kataifi pastry crossways into lengths of about 1 cm and put it in a large bowl.
Pour the melted butter over the pastry. Toss it gently with your hands for about 5 minutes, until every strand is evenly coated.
Spread half the buttered pastry evenly over the bottom of a 25 cm cast-iron frying pan.
Spread the cheese mixture evenly over the pastry, leaving a 1 cm border around the edge.
Layer the rest of the pastry over the cheese and press it down firmly.
Bake for about 40 minutes, until deep golden brown.
While the pastry bakes, make the syrup: put the sugar, lemon juice and 250 ml of water in a saucepan.
Simmer the syrup until it reaches 112°C on a sugar thermometer, or until a little dropped into iced water forms a soft ball. Take it off the heat and leave it to cool.
When the pastry is ready, stir the rose water and orange blossom water into the syrup.
Turn the pastry out onto a serving plate and drizzle it with the syrup. Scatter over the walnuts and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Lamb shawarma
recipes.description: Chunks of leg of lamb marinated in lemon, vinegar, garlic, cinnamon, cardamom and nutmeg, then grilled until golden and served with grilled onions and pitta.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1.5 kg leg of lamb or other tender cut

steps: Cut the lamb into large 4 cm chunks.
Mix the nutmeg, cinnamon, cardamom, garlic, black pepper, cayenne pepper, lemon juice and vinegar in a small bowl and pour it over the meat.
Leave to marinate for at least 2 hours.
Grill the onions with a little garlic for a few minutes.
Drain the meat, pat it dry and grill it until golden brown.
Serve with pitta bread, tomato, fresh onion, tabbouleh, tzatziki, lettuce and chilli sauce.

recipes.title: Musakhan
recipes.description: Palestinian spiced chicken: chicken and onion fried with sumac and black and white pepper, mixed with golden fried nuts, rolled in spring roll pastry and deep-fried.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: sheets, or Arabic village bread (markouk, taboun or tannour)
ingredient_lines.original_text: 10 rolls of either Arabic village bread (markouk, or taboun or tannour) or spring roll pastry

steps: Fry the chicken with the onion.
Add the salt and both peppers before the chicken is cooked through, and add the sumac 5 minutes before the end of cooking.
Fry the nuts until golden, then add them to the chicken and onions.
Roll the mixture up in the spring roll pastry and deep-fry the rolls.
Lift the rolls out of the oil and leave them to drain on kitchen paper.
Serve them hot or cold.

recipes.title: Sabich
recipes.description: An Israeli pitta sandwich of fried aubergine, sliced hard-boiled egg and hummus, topped with a chopped salad and drizzled with tahini and amba.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: For the salad, put the tomatoes, cucumber, onion and parsley in a bowl.
In another small bowl, mix the lemon juice, oil and salt.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables, toss well and leave to stand for a couple of minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. When it is hot enough, fry the aubergine slices until golden brown. Lift them onto kitchen paper to drain off the excess oil.
Spread the hummus evenly inside each pitta bread.
Stuff the pittas with the fried aubergine and the sliced eggs.
Spoon over some of the salad, drizzle the tahini and amba over the pittas, and serve.

recipes.title: Liver kebabs
recipes.description: Moroccan skewers of small cubes of liver marinated with paprika, fresh coriander, garlic and oil, then grilled until charred.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Cut the liver into cubes of about 1 cm and put them in a bowl.
Add the paprika, some salt and pepper, the coriander, garlic and oil.
Mix everything together and leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the liver onto skewers and grill until cooked through and as charred as you like. Serve with fresh bread and a Moroccan salad.

recipes.title: Paella de marisco
recipes.description: Valencian seafood paella: squid, prawns, mussels and langoustines cooked in a wide pan with a tomato sofrito, sweet paprika, saffron and a rich crab and prawn stock.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 500 g yellow onion, cut into quarters

lines.note: or very large crayfish or prawns if you can't find langoustines
lines.original_text: 8 Norway lobsters (or very large crawfish or shrimp if Norway lobsters aren't available)

lines.note: 8–10 strands, or 1½ tsp yellow food colouring
lines.original_text: 8–10 strands of saffron (or 1½ teaspoons food coloring; see notes)

steps: For the stock, boil the stock ingredients in the water until it has reduced to 2 litres. Now and then, press them against the bottom of the pot with a ladle or potato masher to squeeze out their flavour.
Strain the stock and set it aside.
Heat the oil in a 38 cm paella pan over a medium heat. If the pan is bigger than your burner, set it across two and turn it now and then so it cooks evenly.
Add the mussels and cover them with a pan lid: it should cover the mussels but not the whole pan. Cook until they open, then lift them out and set them aside. Throw away any that stay closed.
Add the langoustines and sprinkle each with a pinch of salt.
Sear the langoustines, then lift them out.
Add the squid and fry for about 2 minutes.
Add the prawns and fry for about 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and fry until golden brown, about 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and fry for about 4 minutes to make a sofrito.
Add the rice and stir until it is completely coated in the sofrito.
Add the paprika and fry for about 2 minutes.
Add 2 litres of the seafood stock.
Add the saffron (or food colouring). Mix well and simmer for about 3 minutes.
Taste the broth, and let your guests taste it too. If it is bland, add salt a pinch at a time until everyone is happy.
Put the langoustines and mussels back in and carry on cooking.

Start tasting the rice after it has simmered for about 20 minutes, and turn the heat down a little. Don't let the rice get too soft. Taste it again every 10 minutes, turning the heat down slightly each time. You want rice with a slightly underdone centre. This can take from 30 minutes to an hour, depending on your pan and hob.

The paella is done when the rice is al dente, the paella is a little moist but not soupy, and there is a little toasted rice stuck to the bottom of the pan, a delicacy across the Spanish-speaking world.
Take the pan off the heat and cover it with a clean white tea towel (not foil). Leave it for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Tod mun
recipes.description: Thai fish cakes: minced white fish beaten with red curry paste, egg and sugar, studded with green beans and shredded lime leaves, then fried in spoonfuls until golden.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ cup (120 ml) vegetable oil (for frying)
360 grams (about ¾ lb) ground fish or fish paste (pla kuud)

steps: Stack the lime leaves, roll them into a tube and slice them into thin strips.
Cut the green beans into small pieces of about 1 cm.
Mince the fish.
In a bowl, mix the fish, sugar, salt, curry paste and egg.
Stir until the mixture is smooth.
Add the green beans and lime leaves and stir again.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat.
Drop a tablespoon of the mixture into the pan and flatten it slightly. When the underside is cooked, turn it over.
When both sides are cooked, lift the fish cake onto kitchen paper to drain. Carry on with the rest of the mixture.

recipes.title: Com chien
recipes.description: Vietnamese fried rice, stir-fried with garlic, leeks and red chilli, prawns, carrot, peas and egg, seasoned with chicken stock powder and topped with a fried egg.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan and stir-fry the garlic, chillies and leeks for about 1 minute.
Add the prawns, carrot and peas, then add the beaten eggs. Mix until combined.
Add the rice, salt, pepper and chicken stock powder and stir until well mixed.
Serve with a fried egg on top.

recipes.title: Beans and rice
recipes.description: A cheap Louisiana-style pot of kidney or black beans simmered with onion, pepper, celery, a whole bulb of garlic and cumin, spooned over plain boiled rice.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 package (16 oz) dry beans (kidney or black beans preferred)
1–2 whole dried or fresh hot peppers (optional)

ingredient_lines.note: to cover the beans, plus twice the rice's volume for the rice

steps: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water overnight, or bring them to the boil in a pan of water and leave them to stand for 1 hour. Drain them.
In a large casserole pan or pot, fry the onion and garlic in olive oil over a medium heat until the onion is translucent.
Add the green pepper and celery and fry for a few minutes more.
Add the beans and enough water to cover everything.

Add the bay leaves, cumin, chilli powder, basil and the chillies, if using, then bring to the boil and boil hard for 10 minutes. Lower the heat, cover and simmer, stirring now and then, until the beans are tender (1–2 hours, depending on how old they are). Season with salt and pepper.
Put the rice in a pan with twice its volume of water (240 ml of rice to 480 ml of water).
Bring to a rolling boil and cook until the water has boiled down to the level of the rice.
Turn the heat down to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Serve the beans over the rice. They are also very good with cornbread.

recipes.title: Burgoo
recipes.description: A big Kentucky stew of cooked barbecued meats, chicken and beef stock, potato, okra, sweetcorn, butter beans and peas, simmered slowly for two hours.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or a mix of cooked meats, such as beef, lamb, chicken or game; barbecued is best
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 pound (450 g) mixed cooked meats (beef, lamb, pork, chicken, game, etc.)

steps: Put all the ingredients in a large pot and bring to the boil.
Turn the heat down and simmer for 2 hours, skimming the top as needed.

recipes.title: Cajun burger
recipes.description: Beef burgers coated in Cajun seasoning, grilled, topped with pepper jack and served in buns spread with spiced mayonnaise.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Mix the mayonnaise with 1 tbsp of the Cajun seasoning. Keep it in the fridge until needed.
Shape the mince into 4 equal burgers, 1 cm thick. Sprinkle both sides generously with Cajun seasoning.
Heat the grill. Cook the burgers, turning often, until cooked through with no pink left in the middle (75°C in the centre). Lay a slice of cheese on each burger for the last minute so it melts.
Spread the mayonnaise on the buns and put the burgers in.
Serve straight away.

recipes.title: Cheese enchilada
recipes.description: Corn tortillas softened in a quick chilli gravy, rolled round grated cheddar and onion, then covered with more cheese and gravy and baked briefly.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).

Fry the chilli powder and flour in the oil in a 25–30 cm frying pan until smoothly combined. Add the water, bring to a simmer, then stir for about 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Turn the heat down to low.

Soak one tortilla in the chilli gravy until softened (20–30 seconds). Lift it out of the gravy, lay it flat on a plate and put about 1 tbsp of cheese and 1 tbsp of onion in the centre. Roll it up and lay it seam side down in a 23 x 30 cm baking dish. Repeat until you have used all the tortillas. If the gravy runs low towards the end, stir in 30–60 ml of water.
Cover the enchiladas with the rest of the cheese, onion and chilli gravy.
Bake for about 5 minutes; any longer toughens the cheese.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Homemade wheat tortillas
recipes.description: Soft flour tortillas made from a simple lard dough, kneaded, rolled thin and cooked one at a time in a hot dry frying pan until speckled brown.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1½ cups (360 ml) warm water, or more if needed
4 teaspoons baking powder (optional, for thicker and chewier tortillas)

steps: In a large bowl, stir together the flour, salt and baking powder, if using.
With a pastry blender, a fork or your hands, gradually work in the lard until it is all incorporated.
Add enough warm water to make a soft but not sticky dough.
Turn out on to a lightly floured board and knead for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 90 g portions and shape them into balls.
Roll each ball into a flat round about 15 cm across and 3 mm thick. You can use a tortilla press for this.
Heat a large heavy frying pan over a medium-high heat.
Put the tortillas one at a time into the dry (or very lightly oiled) hot pan. Cook until browned in spots on one side, then turn and brown the other side in spots (about 1 minute a side).
Lift out of the pan and keep warm wrapped in a clean tea towel.

recipes.title: Rice and beef soup
recipes.description: An 1880s soup of cubed beef simmered slowly with long-grain rice, parsley, chives, rosemary and a hint of cinnamon until thick and tender.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 rice cooker cups (12 fl oz / 1½ cups / 360 mL) long grain rice

steps: Put the rice, water, parsley, chives, rosemary, salt and pepper in a large pan that holds at least 3 litres.
Set the pan on the hob over a medium-high heat.
Cover and bring to a simmer.
Add the beef and cinnamon, cover again, turn the heat down low and simmer for 60 minutes, stirring now and then so the rice doesn't stick, until the beef is tender.

recipes.title: Spoonbread
recipes.description: A soft Southern cornmeal pudding with spring onions, chilli flakes and cheese, lightened with whisked egg whites and baked until puffed and just set.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 cup white or yellow corn meal
⅛–1 teaspoon red pepper flakes, to taste

ingredient_lines.note: grated, mild or mature; if using, reduce the salt
ingredient_lines.original_text: ⅓ cup grated cheese, mild or sharp to taste (if used, reduce salt)

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Thickly grease a 20 x 20 cm baking tin with cooking spray or oil.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff, then set aside.
Heat the milk in a medium saucepan over a medium heat until just bubbling at the edges.
Turn the heat down and whisk while slowly adding the cornmeal.
Whisk constantly over a low heat for 5 minutes.
Take off the heat and stir in the black pepper, chilli flakes, salt and spring onions.
Stir in the egg yolks and cheese.
Fold in the whisked egg whites.
Pour into the tin.
Bake for about 30 minutes, or until a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.

recipes.title: Taco casserole
recipes.description: Beef mince browned with taco seasoning, chilli, garlic and passata, then mixed with torn tortillas and plenty of cheese and baked until bubbling.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Brown the beef mince in a frying pan over a medium heat.
Drain off the fat.
Put the mince back in the pan.
Over a medium heat, stir in the taco seasoning, chilli powder, garlic powder and passata.
Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Mix the beef mixture, tortilla pieces and cheese together in an ovenproof dish.
Bake in the oven at 190°C (170°C fan) for 20 minutes.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Basic flapjacks
recipes.description: Chewy British oat bars made by melting butter, light brown sugar and golden syrup together, stirring in porridge oats and baking slowly in a square tin.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 110 g (½ cup or 4 oz) light brown sugar
175 g (1½ cups or 6 oz) rolled oats

steps: Preheat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan).
Put the sugar, butter and golden syrup together in a medium saucepan and heat until the butter has melted.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the oats.
Press the mixture over the base of a lightly greased 19 cm square baking tin.
Bake in the centre of the oven for 40 minutes.
Leave to cool in the tin for 10–15 minutes, then cut into oblong bars.
Leave until cold before taking the flapjacks out of the tin, then store them in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Coronation chicken
recipes.description: The 1953 coronation dish of cold cooked chicken folded through a mild curry mayonnaise with apricot purée, reduced red wine and whipped cream, served with watercress.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: about 2.3 kg, poached and cooled, or other cooked chicken
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 ea. (2.3 kg / 5 lb) chicken, poached (or other cooked chicken)

steps: Skin the chicken if needed and cut it into small pieces. Traditionally the chicken is cooked whole in advance; if you use raw chicken pieces instead, grill them now until cooked through with no pink left (75°C in the centre), then leave them to cool.
Warm the oil in a small saucepan.
Add the onion and cook gently until soft (about 3 minutes).
Add the curry paste, tomato purée, wine, bay leaf and lemon juice. Simmer uncovered for about 10 minutes until well reduced. Strain and leave to cool.
Purée the chopped apricots in a blender or food processor. Beat the cooled sauce into the mayonnaise with the apricot purée.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks and fold it into the mixture.
Season with salt and pepper, and a little more lemon juice if needed.
Fold in the chicken pieces, garnish with watercress and serve.

recipes.title: Friar's omelette
recipes.description: An old Scottish pudding of stewed cooking apples beaten with butter, sugar, lemon and eggs, baked in a dish lined and topped with breadcrumbs, then turned out and dusted with sugar.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 ounces (125 g / 1 stick) butter plus butter for greasing a baking dish
4 ounces (125 g / 1 stick) butter plus butter for greasing a baking dish
1 ounce (25 g / 1 rounded tablespoon) white sugar for decoration

steps: Peel and core the apples, slice them and put them in a saucepan with the water.
Cook until soft, like apple sauce, then take the pan off the heat and add the butter, sugar and lemon juice. Mix well.
While the apple cools, beat the eggs very well. When the apple mixture is cool, mix in the eggs.
Butter a deep baking dish and press breadcrumbs over the base and sides so they stick, keeping a good amount back for the top.
Pour the apple and egg mixture into the dish and cover it with a thick layer of the remaining breadcrumbs.
Bake in a moderate oven at 180°C (160°C fan) for about 30 minutes.
Turn out onto a flat dish and sprinkle with the remaining sugar before serving.

recipes.title: Gingerbread
recipes.description: A soft, sticky gingerbread cake made with melted butter, brown sugar and golden syrup, spiced with ginger and mixed spice, baked in a square tin and left a day before cutting.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Put the butter, sugar and golden syrup in a saucepan and heat gently until the butter melts.
Put the flour, baking powder, mixed spice and ginger in a bowl. Pour in the melted butter mixture and beat thoroughly.
Warm the milk in a saucepan, so that it will dissolve the syrup.
Add the milk to the bowl and beat thoroughly.
Beat the eggs, then stir them into the mixture.
Grease a 20 cm square cake tin with butter and pour in the mixture.
Bake at 170°C (150°C fan) for 1 hour.
Leave to cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then turn out.
Leave for at least a day before cutting into squares and serving.

recipes.title: Lentil, barley, and tomato soup
recipes.description: Alexandra soup: lentils and pearl barley simmered with butter-softened onion until tender, finished with fresh tomatoes and puréed into a smooth, warming bowl.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: If you like, soak the lentils and barley together overnight, then drain them.
Fry the onion in the butter in a large saucepan until soft.
Add the lentils, barley and water.
Simmer until the lentils are tender. This takes longer if they haven't been soaked.
Add the tomatoes when the soup is almost ready.
Purée the soup with a food mill, blender or food processor.
Reheat, and season to taste with salt and pepper.

recipes.title: North Staffordshire oatcakes
recipes.description: The Potteries' own oatcakes: a yeasted batter of fine oatmeal and flour left to rise, then cooked on a hot griddle into large, soft, holey pancakes for filling with cheese, bacon or egg.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 220 g (1 cup or 8 oz) fine oatmeal
220 g (1 cup or 8 oz) wholemeal or plain flour
14 g (2 ½ tsp or ½ oz) fresh yeast
850 ml (3 ½ cups or 1 ½ pints) warm milk and water, mixed half and half
850 ml (3 ½ cups or 1 ½ pints) warm milk and water, mixed half and half

steps: Mix the salt into the flour and oatmeal.
Dissolve the yeast in a little of the warm milk and water and add the sugar. Leave until frothy.
Mix the dry ingredients with the yeast liquid and the rest of the milk and water to make a batter.
Cover the batter with a clean cloth and leave it in a warm place for an hour.
Grease a griddle well with oil and heat it. Pour on enough batter to make an oatcake about 20–23 cm across. The surface will be covered in holes as it cooks.

After 2–3 minutes, when the top looks dry and the underside is golden brown, turn the oatcake over and cook for another 2–3 minutes. Carry on with the rest of the batter, greasing the griddle again as needed.

recipes.title: Pease pudding
recipes.description: A North East favourite: yellow split peas cooked in the stock from a ham hock in a pressure cooker, whisked with butter and left to set, for spreading on bread or stotties with the ham.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 uncooked ham hock or ham joint (from a butcher shop)

steps: Put the ham hock in a pressure cooker and cover it with water.
Put the lid on and bring to the boil (full pressure).
Turn the heat down and simmer for 30–40 minutes.
Take the cooker off the heat and release the pressure. Lift out the hock and set it aside.
Add the split peas to the cooking liquid.
Put the lid back on and bring back to the boil.
Turn the heat down again to a simmer, as low as it will go.
Simmer for 25–30 minutes.
Take the cooker off the heat and release the pressure.
Tip the contents into a bowl with the butter and mix with a balloon whisk.
Leave to cool.
Serve on white bread or stottie cake, on its own or with ham from the hock. Keep it in the fridge once cool.

recipes.title: Trifle
recipes.description: A classic layered sherry trifle: slices of Swiss roll soaked in sherry, topped with peaches, fruit jelly, custard and whipped double cream, finished with hundreds and thousands.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 swiss roll or similar sponge cake
1 packet/sachet fruit-flavoured jelly (can be found under the brand names "Quick-Jel" or "Jell-O")

ingredient_lines.note: fresh or made from custard powder
or sprinkles or other sweet topping
ingredient_lines.original_text: Hundreds and thousands, sprinkles, or other sweet topping (optional)

steps: Cut the Swiss roll into slices about 2 cm thick and line the base of a glass serving dish with them.
Pour the sherry over the Swiss roll.
Drain the peaches, keeping the juice or syrup, and arrange them over the Swiss roll.
Make up the jelly following the packet instructions; you can use the syrup from the peaches as part of the liquid. Pour the jelly into the dish and leave it in the fridge to set.

Make the custard, again following its instructions (use fresh custard or custard powder rather than tinned). Leave it to cool until lukewarm, then pour it over the jelly. Leave it in the fridge to set.
Whip the cream and spread it over the custard. Decorate with hundreds and thousands or other sweet toppings.
Serve.

recipes.title: Arroz con maiz
recipes.description: Puerto Rican rice with sweetcorn: medium-grain rice cooked in annatto oil with a fresh blended sofrito, sliced Vienna sausages, toasted cumin and coriander, white wine and stock.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 2 medium yellow onions, cut into large chunks
3–4 Italian frying peppers (also know as cubanelle peppers)

lines.note: leaves, or another handful of coriander
lines.original_text: 10 leaves of culantro (recao), or another handful of cilantro

lines.note: ripe, seeded, cored and cut into chunks (or roasted, with skin and seeds removed)
lines.original_text: 3–4 ripe plum tomatoes, seeded, cored, and cut into chunks (or roasted with skin and seeds removed)

lines.note: large, cored, seeded and cut into large chunks (or roasted, with seeds and some skin removed)
lines.original_text: 1 large red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and cut into large chunks (or roasted with seeds and some skin removed)
⅓ cup olive oil or butter

lines.note: alcaparrado (manzanilla olives with pimiento and capers)
lines.original_text: 2 tablespoons Alcaparrado (manzanilla olives, pimientos, and capers)
3 teaspoons cumin seeds or ground cumin
1½ teaspoons coriander seeds or ground coriander

lines.note: 200 g, Vienna sausages, sliced, liquid kept
lines.original_text: 1 can (5 oz) Vienna sausage, sliced with liquid saved

lines.note: frozen, tinned or fresh (if fresh, cooked and cut from the cob ahead of time)
lines.original_text: ¼ cup frozen, canned, or fresh corn kernels. If using fresh corn, cook and remove corn from cob ahead of time

lines.note: or another medium-grain rice, not rinsed
lines.original_text: 3 cups medium grain rice (do not rinse)

steps: For the sofrito, chop the onions, put them in a blender and blend until liquid.
With the motor running, add the rest of the sofrito ingredients one at a time and blend until smooth.
Set aside 360 ml of the sofrito for the rice. The rest keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze it in ice cube trays for up to a month.

For the rice, heat the oil and annatto seeds in a small frying pan over a medium heat just until the seeds give off a lively, steady sizzle. Don't overheat them, or the seeds will turn black and the oil green. Once they are sizzling, take the pan off the heat and leave it until the sizzling stops.
Strain as much of the oil as you can into a heavy pot or casserole and leave it to stand for at least 5 minutes.
Lightly toast the cumin and coriander seeds in a small frying pan over a low heat for a few minutes. Keep an eye on them, as they darken fast.
Take the seeds off the heat and grind them in a spice grinder or coffee mill.

Reheat the annatto oil over a high heat until it shimmers. Stir in the sausages and brown them. Add the 360 ml of sofrito, the alcaparrado, salt, bay leaves, ground coriander and cumin, and pepper. Cook until the sofrito stops bubbling and sizzles, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice until everything is mixed together and the rice is coated all over with oil.

Stir in the wine, the liquid from the sausages and enough stock or water to cover the rice by two fingers' width. Lay the banana leaf on top (or use a pan lid), folding or cutting it to fit over the rice.
Bring to the boil, then boil without stirring until the liquid has sunk to the level of the rice.

Lift off the banana leaf, give the rice a big stir and put the leaf back on top. Turn the heat down to low, cover the pot with its lid and cook until the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
When the rice is cooked, mix in the sweetcorn, cover and cook for 1 minute more.

recipes.title: Jamaican banana fritters
recipes.description: Little Jamaican fritters of mashed ripe banana, flour, milk, sugar and vanilla, dropped by the spoonful into hot oil and fried golden on both sides, to eat hot as a snack or pudding.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Peel the bananas and mash them in a bowl until runny.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over a medium heat.
Add the sugar, milk, vanilla, salt, baking powder and flour to the bananas and mix until about as thick as pancake batter, or a little thinner.
Drop tablespoons of the mixture into the hot oil and fry until the edges are firm, then turn them over and fry the other side until golden brown.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot.

recipes.title: Jamaican curry chicken with bulla
recipes.description: Chicken pieces rinsed in lime, tossed with spring onions, onions, red chillies and plenty of Jamaican curry powder, then cooked slowly in olive oil and served with sweet bulla cakes.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: Just over ½ cup olive oil

steps: Cut the chicken into pieces of the same size.
Rinse the chicken in lime juice.
Mix the chicken with the spring onions, onions, chillies, curry powder, salt and pepper. Cover and leave to marinate in the fridge for 5–10 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a pot. Add the chicken mixture and cook, stirring now and then, for 30–60 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink left in the middle.
Serve with bulla cakes.

recipes.title: Phulourie
recipes.description: Caribbean split pea fritters: soaked yellow split peas ground with garlic, turmeric and cumin into a soft batter, dropped in small balls into hot oil and fried golden, to eat with dhal or a sour chutney.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or 450 g ground split pea flour
ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ pt split peas, or 1 lb ground split pea flour

ingredient_lines.note: cold, for soaking, plus enough to make the batter

steps: If you are using whole split peas, soak them overnight in lightly salted cold water. Drain them and grind them finely in a mill or food processor.
Mix all the ingredients, adding enough water to make a batter with a dropping consistency.
Heat the oil for deep-frying. Drop dollops of batter into the hot oil, squeezing them between your thumb and forefinger to make balls about 2 cm across.
Fry until golden brown and cooked through, then lift them out of the oil and drain them on brown paper or kitchen paper.

recipes.title: Roasted pork shoulder
recipes.description: Puerto Rican pernil: a whole pork shoulder studded with a pounded paste of garlic, oregano, thyme, oil and vinegar, left in the fridge for days, then slow-roasted until the meat pulls apart and the skin crackles.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Pat the pork shoulder dry with kitchen paper. Don't wash it: splashing raw pork spreads bacteria around the kitchen.
Lay the pork skin side down and, with a sharp knife, make deep cuts in it in different places.
Grind the garlic, pepper, oregano, thyme and salt together, using a mortar and pestle.
When they are ground, mix in the oil and vinegar.
Fill the cuts in the pork with the mixture, and rub whatever is left over the outside.
Cover the pork and leave it in the fridge for 3 days. If you want to cook it the same day, prepare it at least 1 hour ahead and keep it in the fridge until needed.
Take the pork out of the fridge 2 hours before it goes in the oven.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) for at least 10 minutes before the pork goes in.
Put the pork in a roasting tin and roast for 3½ hours.
Turn the oven up to 190°C (170°C fan) and roast for 15–30 minutes more, until the skin is crisp and browned.

recipes.title: Prawn fritters
recipes.description: Trinidadian accra: chopped prawns, green pepper, spring onion, garlic and Scotch bonnet beaten into a soft, herby flour batter and dropped by the spoonful into hot oil until puffed and brown.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: ¼ cup (60 ml) green pepper, chopped

ingredient_lines.note: or another hot chilli, finely chopped
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 Scotch bonnet or other hot pepper, minced

ingredient_lines.note: enough to make a soft batter

steps: Mix the green pepper, spring onions, onion and Scotch bonnet in a bowl.
Add the rest of the ingredients except the water and oil, and mix thoroughly.
Stir in enough water with a spoon to make a soft batter, then beat until smooth.
Heat the oil in a deep pan or deep-fat fryer. Drop in spoonfuls of the batter and fry, turning, until brown on all sides and the prawns are cooked through.

recipes.title: Taro fish
recipes.description: A vegetarian Chinese centrepiece: steamed taro mashed with stock powder, rolled in nori and snipped into a fish shape, then scored and dressed with stir-fried pepper, ginger, spring onion, black beans and Shaoxing wine.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: a little, to soak the black beans

steps: Peel the taro and cut it into 3 cm chunks. Steam until soft.
Meanwhile, soak the black beans in a little water.
Mash the taro with the vegetable stock powder.
Lay the 2 nori sheets on the work surface, overlapping, and dampen one so they stick together.
Put the mashed taro in the middle of the sheets and roll the nori over the top.
Cut the nori at one end to look like a fish's fins.
Cut the green pepper, ginger and spring onions into thin strips and stir-fry them in a little oil in a wok or frying pan for a few minutes.
Add the Shaoxing wine and the black beans.
Make cuts halfway through the taro fish at intervals of about 3 cm, and pour the sauce over it.
Serve on a platter.

recipes.title: Alsatian chicken fricassée
recipes.description: Skinless chicken pieces baked in a whole bottle of red wine with bacon, mushrooms, plenty of onion, garlic and herbs, the sauce thickened at the end and the dish finished with chopped parsley.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Remove the skin from the chicken and season all the pieces with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a flameproof casserole on the hob.
Fry the bacon until its fat runs, then add the onions.
Add the garlic and mushrooms, then the chicken. Pour in the wine and add the parsley sprigs, thyme and bay leaves.
Bake for about 45 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink left at the bone.
A few minutes before the end, mix the flour with the olive oil and stir it into the liquid in the casserole, turning the chicken pieces so they are well coated in the sauce.
Sprinkle the chicken with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.title: Baguette
recipes.description: Classic French sticks made over a long day: a simple yeasted dough rested, kneaded and risen three times, shaped into long loaves, slashed and baked hot on a stone with a burst of steam for a crackling crust.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: Very warm water (105–115°F): ¼ cup, 2 ounces (59.25 g)
Unbleached all-purpose flour: 4 cups, 18 ounces (500 g)

ingredient_lines.note: very hot, for the oven, plus more for misting

steps: Stir the yeast into the warm water in a small bowl with a fork until it dissolves. Leave for 3 minutes.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl.
Gently mix the cool water, the yeast mixture and the flour with your fingers until they come together in a mass.
Knead on a lightly floured work surface for 5 minutes. The dough should now be supple and springy.
Cover the dough with cling film or a light tea towel.
Leave it to rest for 25 minutes. This rest is called the autolyse.
Knead the dough for 6–8 minutes more, until it is smooth and stretchy. Don't overdo it, or the dough will be tough.
Lightly oil a bowl and turn the dough in it to coat it with oil. Cover the bowl with a tea towel.
Leave to rise at room temperature (about 24°C) for 1½–2 hours, until doubled in size.
Gently knock back the dough, fold it over itself and shape it into a ball again. Cover with the tea towel.
Leave to rise for 1¼ hours, or until doubled again.
Gently knock back the dough once more, shape it into a round, cover and leave to rise for about 1 hour.
On a lightly floured surface, divide the dough into 3 equal pieces, about 290 g each.
Gently stretch one piece into a rectangle, keeping some large bubbles in the dough.
Fold the top third down and the bottom third up.
Roll the dough over from left to right into a log, sealing the seam with the heel of your hand.
Fold the dough over about a third of the way each time, seal along the length of the loaf, and repeat.
The aim is to draw the skin gently tight over the surface while keeping some air bubbles inside. Seal the seam, taking care not to tear the skin or knock the air out.
Leave the loaf on the work surface to relax before lengthening it, and shape the other pieces of dough the same way.

Now lengthen each baguette, starting with the first one you shaped, by rolling it back and forth on the work surface. Start with both hands over the middle and work them out to the ends until the loaf is as long as you want, but no longer than your oven allows.
Put the loaves on a peel or an upturned baking tray lined with baking paper and sprinkled generously with polenta, or in a baguette tin.

Cover with well-oiled cling film or a floured cloth and leave to rise for 30–40 minutes, until slightly plump but not doubled. The short final rise leaves the loaves slightly under-proved, which gives a better oven spring, a light, airy crumb and cuts that open out more.
Thirty minutes before baking, preheat the oven to 260°C (240°C fan).
Put a baking stone in the oven to heat, with an empty roasting tin on the shelf directly below it.

With a very sharp razor blade or baker's lame, make 3–5 slashes along the top of each baguette, depending on its length. The cuts should run along the loaf from one end to the other rather than across it, with the blade held at a 30° angle so they open in the oven. Don't press too hard, or you may knock the air out.
Mist the loaves with a water spray bottle.

Gently slide the loaves onto the hot stone, or put the baguette tin in the oven. Pour 240 ml of very hot water into the tin below and quickly close the oven door. After 1 minute, mist the loaves and the oven walls 6–8 times and close the door. After 2 more minutes, mist them again.
Bake for 12 minutes, then turn the oven down to 200°C (180°C fan) and bake for 25–30 minutes more, until the loaves are golden brown and crisp. Move them to a wire rack to cool.
Enjoy the baguettes still slightly warm, with a soft, ripe French cheese and a glass of wine.

recipes.title: Cod, olive oil, and cream sauce
recipes.description: Brandade de morue from Nîmes: salt cod soaked for a day, poached and puréed with softened onion, garlic, olive oil, milk or cream and lemon into a smooth, rich spread for toast or roast potato slices.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 lb salt cod, skinless and boneless

ingredient_lines.note: or double cream, plus more to thin
ingredient_lines.original_text: ½ cup milk or heavy cream
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, or to taste
2 cloves garlic, pressed or grated with a microplane

ingredient_lines.note: to soak and poach the cod
sliced, to serve instead of toast

steps: Put the salt cod in a large bowl of cold water.
Leave it to soak in the fridge for 24 hours, changing the water several times. When the fish has fully rehydrated, it is ready.
Poach the cod in plain water for 25 minutes, or until it flakes easily.
Drain it and break it into pieces.
Cook the onion in a little of the olive oil over a low heat until translucent.
In a food processor, purée the cod, onion and garlic with half of the olive oil.
With the motor running, add the milk or cream, the rest of the oil, the lemon juice and the pepper.
Blend until smooth. If it is too thick, thin it with a little more milk or cream.
Serve on toast, or on slices of potato coated in olive oil and roasted in the oven at 200°C (180°C fan) for 30–40 minutes, turning once.

recipes.title: Le tourin
recipes.description: A garlic soup from the Dordogne: a dozen cloves browned in olive oil, thickened with a little flour and water, enriched with egg and a dash of vinegar, then poured over thin slices of bread.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Brown the chopped garlic in the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan.
Add the flour. Mix well, then cook for a few minutes to cook out the raw flour taste.
Gradually stir in the water, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Beat the egg white in a small bowl. Gradually whisk in a ladleful of the soup to temper it, then stir the mixture back into the pan.
Mix the egg yolk, pepper and vinegar in another small bowl, and temper it with a ladleful of soup in the same way.

Take the soup off the heat and stir in the egg yolk mixture. Put it back on a low heat and stir for 1–2 minutes, until the egg is cooked and the soup is piping hot, without letting it boil. Season to taste with salt.
