Put thin slices of bread in each soup bowl and pour the soup over them. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Potatoes with green sauce
recipes.description: Frankfurt's grüne Soße: soured cream loosened with milk, oil and lemon, packed with dill, chives and other fresh herbs and chopped hard-boiled egg, chilled and spooned cold over hot boiled potatoes.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 3–4 cups (200 g / 7 oz per cup) sour cream
1 tbsp sunflower oil (or other oil of neutral taste)

ingredient_lines.note: finely chopped, 1–1½ soured cream tubs (200 g size) full
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1–1½ empty sour cream cups filled with dill

ingredient_lines.note: finely chopped, or a mix with parsley, spring onion tops, lemon balm, salad burnet and a little sorrel
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1–1½ empty sour cream cups filled with other mixed herbs (e.g. chives, parsley, onion leaves, lemon balm, burnet, a small amount of sorrel if available)

steps: Mix the soured cream, oil and lemon juice. Add milk until the mixture is the consistency of a thick sauce.
Mix the herbs together well, and stir them into the sauce.
Chop the hard-boiled eggs into small pieces and add them to the sauce with some salt and pepper.
Leave the sauce in the fridge for about 1–1½ hours.
Boil the potatoes and serve them hot with the cold sauce. You can serve more hard-boiled eggs alongside.

recipes.title: Chicken curry
recipes.description: A big, warmly spiced curry: chicken marinated in coconut yoghurt and a long list of spices, seared, then simmered with tomatoes, potatoes and onion fried with mustard, cumin and fennel seeds.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.note: a little, to sear the chicken

steps: Clean the chicken and cut it into small pieces. Mix it well with all the marinade ingredients, cover and leave in the fridge for 30 minutes so the flavours soak in.
Heat the coconut oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and fry the cumin, fennel and mustard seeds.
Add the garlic and ginger paste and fry.
Chop the onion into small pieces and fry it in the pan.
Add the potatoes and fry.
In a separate pan, sear the chicken in batches in a little oil, and set it aside in a bowl.
When the onion is golden brown, add the chicken.
Add the curry powder, tomatoes and coconut yoghurt and turn the heat down low. Cook for 35–40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
Stir in some finely chopped fresh coriander and a dash of lemon juice.
Serve with rice or naan bread.

recipes.title: Chicken tikka
recipes.description: Cubes of chicken breast marinated for a day or two in yoghurt, lemon, garlic, fresh red chilli and warm spices with a little mustard oil, then threaded onto skewers and grilled until charred at the edges.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: skinless and boneless, cut into cubes
ingredient_lines.original_text: 675 g (1.5 lb) skinless and boneless chicken breast, diced into cubes

ingredient_lines.note: or crackle 1 tsp mustard seeds in 2 tbsp very hot vegetable or olive oil and leave to cool

ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 large cloves of garlic, finely chopped

ingredient_lines.note: fresh, chopped, depending on their heat and how hot you want the marinade
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1–4 chopped fresh red chillis (depending on strength of the chillis and the desired strength of the marinade)
1 tsp salt (use rock salt for best results)

steps: Put all the ingredients except the chicken in a non-metallic mixing bowl, and mix well.
Add the chicken and mix until it is fully coated.

Ideally, cover the bowl and leave the chicken in the fridge to marinate for at least 24 hours. Chicken that has been frozen before may not be safe to leave for longer than 24 hours, but fresh chicken is best left for 48 hours. If you don't want to marinate it, go straight on to the next step.

Thread the chicken onto skewers. For the best results, cook it in a tandoor or a ceramic pot oven; otherwise cook it under a medium grill for 5–8 minutes on each side, or on a barbecue (the time depends on the heat of the barbecue). Always make sure the chicken is cooked through before serving: it should come apart easily when pressed with the side of a fork, with no pink left.
Serve with naan or rice, or use it in a chicken tikka masala.

recipes.title: Jalebi
recipes.description: Loops of tangy batter, left to ferment overnight, piped into hot oil, fried until golden and dipped in a rose-scented orange sugar syrup.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 3 cups of vegetable oil/ghee for deep frying

steps: Mix the flour, gram flour, baking powder and water until smooth.
Leave the batter uncovered at room temperature overnight (about 12 hours).
For the syrup, mix the sugar, water and cream of tartar in a saucepan.
Stir the syrup over a medium heat until the sugar has dissolved.
Turn the heat up to high and boil for 5 minutes.
Leave the syrup to cool, then stir in the rose water. Tint it light orange with the food colouring.
Heat the oil in a wide wok or similar pan to about 175°C.
Spoon the batter into a piping bag with an opening of about 1 cm. If it is too stiff to squeeze out, mix in a little water.
Squeeze the batter into the oil in a couple of figures of eight and loops on top of each other, about 8 cm on the longest side.
Fry each jalebi until golden brown. Lift it out, let the oil drain off, then soak it in the syrup for a minute.
Serve.

recipes.title: Malvani chicken curry
recipes.description: A Konkan-coast chicken curry from Maharashtra: pieces on the bone marinated in green chilli, ginger and garlic, then simmered in a paste of toasted coconut and onion with Malvani masala.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 800 g (1.8 lb / 8 ea.) medium-sized pieces of chicken

steps: Grind half the green chillies to a paste and mix it well with the ginger and garlic pastes.
Make cuts in the chicken pieces and rub the paste well into them. Cover and leave to marinate in the fridge for at least an hour.
Toast the coconut in a frying pan with a little hot oil until light brown. Leave it to cool, then grind it with half the onions to a paste in a blender.
Heat the rest of the oil in a heavy-based pan and fry the remaining onions over a medium heat for about 2 minutes, until light brown.

Add the rest of the green chillies, the chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala and Malvani masala and fry for a few seconds. Add the marinated chicken and fry over a medium heat for about 3 minutes, until lightly browned.

Add the coconut paste and the salt and mix well. Add as much water as you need for the consistency you like and bring to the boil. Cover and cook over a low heat for about 25 minutes, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Garnish with the coriander.

recipes.title: Pigeon pea and fenugreek curry
recipes.description: Methi tadka dal: toor dal pressure-cooked with fenugreek leaves, tomato, onion and green chilli, then stirred into a sizzling tempering of ghee, mustard seeds, cumin, garlic and curry leaves.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 2 handfuls of methi leaves (only the leaves without the tender stem)
½ small spoon of mustard seeds

steps: Put the dal, water, fenugreek leaves, the 3 tomatoes, onion, turmeric, green chillies, peppercorns, butter and ginger (if using) in a pressure cooker. Cook until the dal is soft (4 whistles).
Heat the ghee in a pan and add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, garlic, red chillies and curry leaves. Fry until the garlic is golden.
Add the chopped tomato, then salt, chilli powder and ground coriander to taste.
Add the cooked dal mixture to the pan and leave it to simmer. Add a little water if you like it more like a gravy.
Add a couple of drops of lemon juice.
Serve with hot rice, and a little Gongura pickle if you like.

recipes.title: Potato curry
recipes.description: South Indian aloo masala: par-boiled potatoes cooked down with mustard seeds, curry leaves, onion, green chillies and turmeric until soft, for dosa or roti.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan.
Fry the mustard seeds first, then add the chana dal, curry leaves, onion and chillies.
Fry until the onions begin to change colour.
Add the potatoes.
Sprinkle over the turmeric evenly and stir well to mix everything.
Cover and cook over a medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring well, until the potatoes are very soft and partly mashed.
Season with the salt to taste.

recipes.title: Puri
recipes.description: Small rounds of wholemeal and semolina dough, deep-fried until they puff up into golden, hollow breads.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 tbsp vegetable oil for the dough
About 500 ml (1 pint) vegetable oil for deep frying

steps: Put the wholemeal flour, plain flour and semolina in a bowl.
Add the salt and drizzle over the 1 tbsp of oil. Mix well.
Gradually mix in enough water to make a stiff dough.
Knead the dough well for a few minutes.
Cover the dough and leave it to rest for about half an hour.
Pour the oil for deep-frying into a wok or other deep pan and heat it.
Meanwhile, divide the dough into 8 small balls and roll each into a small circle about 7.5 cm across. Rub a little of the hot oil on the rolling surface so the dough doesn't stick.

Check the oil is hot enough: a tiny piece of dough dropped in should rise to the surface straight away. If it sinks to the bottom, the oil is not hot enough and the puri will soak up too much oil. When the oil is ready, lay a circle of dough on it and press the top lightly with a slotted spoon until it puffs up, then turn it over. Adjust the heat as you go.
Lift the puri out of the oil when it is golden brown and leave it on a wire rack or kitchen paper to drain.

recipes.title: Rasam
recipes.description: A thin, peppery South Indian soup of tomatoes and tamarind with a little toor dal and freshly toasted rasam powder, finished with a mustard seed and curry leaf tempering and spooned over rice.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 14 g (½ oz) toovar dhal (also called red gram dhal)
1 tsp sugar (jaggery or palm sugar is good too)

lines.note: plenty: rasam is meant to be very thin
lines.original_text: Water—the amount depends on the amount of rasam required as it is meant to be very watery.
1 tsp urad dhal or cumin seeds

steps: For the rasam powder, fry the coriander seeds, chillies and cumin seeds together in the oil or ghee in a frying pan, adding the asafoetida last. Toast until the spices start to brown slightly.
Grind everything to a powder in a spice grinder or blender. Coriander seeds are very hard to grind fine.
For the dal, wash the toor dal well until the water runs clear.

Cover it with twice its volume of water and add the turmeric and the 1 tsp of oil. Cook it covered, slowly on the hob, or for half an hour in the microwave, or in a pressure cooker, until it is mushy.
Cut the tomatoes into quarters, put them in a saucepan full of water and bring to the boil.
Add the tamarind, salt and sugar. Tamarind is usually very sharp, so add only a little at a time; you can add more later to adjust the flavour.
When the tomatoes are half cooked, add the cooked dal.
Add enough rasam powder to give the taste you want, usually 4–5 tsp. It should be fairly spicy, with neither the tamarind nor the sugar standing out. Stir and keep simmering.

For the tempering, heat the ghee in a small pan and add the mustard seeds, urad dal, chillies and curry leaves. The dal should start to brown and the mustard seeds to splutter. Don't let any of the spices burn; it's easy to do. As soon as they are done, pour the tempering into the rasam and stir it through.
Add the chopped coriander. Serve with hot, soft, plain boiled rice.

recipes.title: Pasta with pancetta and cauliflower
recipes.description: Pasta tossed with crisp pancetta, blanched cauliflower, garlic, chilli and tomatoes, then bound with a silky sauce of egg yolks and pecorino.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 head (~500 g / 1.1 pound) cauliflower, cut into florets
1 can (14 ounces / 400 g) diced tomatoes, drained
½ cup (60 g / 2.1 ounces) grated Pecorino Romano cheese
Chopped parsley, additional grated Pecorino Romano cheese
Chopped parsley, additional grated Pecorino Romano cheese

steps: Bring 3.8 litres of water to the boil in a large pot. Add the cauliflower and cook for 4 minutes. Lift it out into a bowl of iced water, keeping the cooking water in the pot.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. When it is hot, add the pancetta and start to brown it.
Once the pancetta begins to brown, add the pasta to the boiling water.

When the pancetta is almost completely browned, turn the heat down to medium and add the garlic and chilli flakes. Fry until the garlic starts to turn golden, then add the drained cauliflower and the tomatoes and toss to heat through. Add 60 ml of the pasta water, and salt and pepper.
While the pasta finishes cooking, beat the egg yolks, grated pecorino, salt and pepper until smooth.
When the pasta is about 2 minutes away from al dente, drain it.
Turn the heat under the sauce down to low, add the pasta and toss to combine. Pour over the egg yolk mixture and toss the pasta quickly to coat it; the yolks should coat the pasta, not scramble.

Keep tossing over the low heat until the sauce has thickened and the pasta is piping hot all the way through, then tip it into a serving bowl or onto plates and garnish with the parsley and more pecorino.

recipes.title: Rice and turnip minestrone
recipes.description: An old Lombard soup of salted turnip slices softened in butter with tomatoes and gravy, then boiled in stock with a little rice.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or beef or vegetable stock, brought to the boil
ingredient_lines.original_text: 4 cups chicken, beef, or vegetable stock, brought to a boil

steps: Arrange the turnip slices on a rack over a baking tray. Sprinkle them with salt, cover with a plate and leave for about 2 hours, until the water has run out of them.
Put the slices in a frying pan and fry them gently in butter until softened.
Add the gravy and tomatoes and cook for a few minutes. Meanwhile, bring the stock to the boil in a large saucepan, then pour the turnip mixture into the boiling stock.
Add the rice and boil for 30 minutes; don't boil it much longer, or the soup loses its flavour. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Daigakuimo
recipes.description: Japanese candied sweet potato: bite-sized pieces deep-fried until golden, then tossed in a sticky soy and sugar glaze and scattered with sesame seeds.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured
steps: Cut the sweet potatoes into bite-sized pieces.
Heat the oil to 175°C and fry the sweet potatoes until brown. Lift them out and drain them on kitchen paper.
Mix the water, sugar and soy sauce in a saucepan and put it over a low heat.
When the liquid turns sticky, take it off the heat and add the fried sweet potatoes. Quickly toss them in the sticky syrup to coat.
Sprinkle the sesame seeds over the coated sweet potatoes.

recipes.title: Camotes enmielados
recipes.description: A Mexican home-cooked dessert of sweet potato baked under a cone of piloncillo with cinnamon sticks, basted until it sits in a dark, syrupy caramel.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: large, or a yam; peeled if you like
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 large yam or sweet potato, optionally peeled

ingredient_lines.note: large cone; or another dark unrefined sugar, such as muscovado or jaggery

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Put the sweet potato, whole or in thick slices, in a large baking dish.
Put the piloncillo on top of the sweet potato, then add the water and cinnamon.
Cover the dish with a lid or foil and bake for about 60 minutes, basting the sweet potato with the sweetened cooking liquid as needed.

recipes.title: Beef and vegetable kebabs
recipes.description: Cubes of sirloin marinated in smoked paprika, cayenne, balsamic vinegar and fresh herbs, threaded onto skewers with onion, peppers and courgette and grilled over a high heat.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 ½ pounds (about 700 g) beef sirloin, cut into 1 ½ inch (4 cm) cubes

ingredient_lines.note: several, in assorted colours, cut into 7.5 cm strips
ingredient_lines.original_text: Several assorted bell peppers, cut into 3-inch (7.5 cm) strips

steps: Put the paprika, salt, pepper, cayenne pepper, olive oil, rosemary, thyme and balsamic vinegar in a large (4 litre) food bag and mix. Add the beef, seal and leave in the fridge for at least 1 hour. Meanwhile, soak 6 bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes.

Sort the beef cubes into rows of equal size. On each skewer, thread 1 onion wedge, 1 strip of pepper, 1 slice of courgette through its side and 3 cubes of beef across the grain, repeating the pattern.
Grill over a medium-high heat, on a barbecue or under the grill, turning often, for 11 minutes for medium. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Cypriot salad
recipes.description: The everyday village salad of Cyprus: tomato, cucumber and lettuce in a bowl, topped with onion, feta and black olives and dressed with olive oil and lemon juice just before it goes to the table.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 spoon of feta cheese, cut into small pieces

steps: Cut the tomato, cucumber, lettuce and onion into pieces.
Put the tomato, cucumber and lettuce in a bowl and top with the onion, feta and olives, arranged however you like.
Just before serving, pour over the olive oil and lemon juice and toss the salad.

recipes.title: Garlic and lemon chicken
recipes.description: A Lebanese slow bake: chicken breasts marinated overnight in lemon, garlic and cayenne, browned, then cooked low for hours with sliced potatoes and served with toom, a sharp whipped garlic sauce.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.original_text: 4 chicken breasts, boneless and with skin
6 large potatoes, sliced ¼ inch thick

steps: Mix the lemon juice, garlic, salt, pepper, basil and cayenne pepper to make a marinade.
Put the chicken breasts in a deep ovenproof dish and pour the marinade over them.
Cover and leave to marinate in the fridge overnight. In the morning, turn the chicken over and marinate it for another 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Drain the marinade from the dish and keep it. Bake the chicken for 10 to 15 minutes to brown it, without cooking it through.
Pour the marinade back over the browned chicken. Cover the dish tightly with foil and put it back in the oven.
Turn the oven down to 120°C (100°C fan). Bake the chicken for 4 hours, basting it with the marinade every hour.
Add the sliced potatoes to the dish, baste everything and cover it with the foil again.
Put it back in the oven and cook for another hour, until the potatoes are tender and the chicken is cooked through, at least 75°C in the thickest part.
When the chicken is in its last hour in the oven, blend all the toom ingredients in a food processor until smooth.
Serve the chicken and potatoes with the toom and some warm pitta bread.

recipes.title: Gözleme
recipes.description: Turkish flatbread: a soft yeasted dough rolled thin, brushed with oil, folded around a filling such as spinach and feta, sealed and browned in butter on a hot griddle.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: finely chopped, for the filling, or another filling

steps: Sift the flour into a large bowl, keeping back 125 g of it.
Sprinkle over the salt and mix. Make a well in the centre.
Mix the yeast and sugar in a small bowl. Stir in 60 ml of the warm water.
Pour the yeast mixture into the well in the flour.
Cover the yeast with a little of the flour and leave for 10 minutes to rise.
Stir in the rest of the water, mixing thoroughly. Knead for 5 minutes to make a medium-soft dough.
Cover and leave to rise somewhere warm for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Put the dough on a board dusted with some of the kept-back flour. With floured hands, divide it into 10 pieces.
Shape each piece into a ball, then roll it out with a rolling pin into a rectangle 5 mm thick. Brush with oil.
Fold two opposite edges over so they meet in the centre.
Spread the spinach and feta (or another filling, such as minced beef, potato or cheese) over half of the dough, then fold the other half over the filling to make an oblong.
Seal the edges well, pressing lightly.
Heat a griddle or a cast-iron frying pan.
Grease it with butter and put in a gözleme.
Brown it on both sides, then repeat with the rest, greasing the pan each time.
Serve hot, with ayran to drink.

recipes.title: Lamb and okra stew
recipes.description: Khoresht bamiye, a Persian stew of lamb simmered with golden onions until tender, then finished with okra, tomato purée and a squeeze of lime, served over white rice.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: or stewing beef, cut into small pieces
ingredient_lines.original_text: 500 grams stewing lamb or beef, cut into small pieces
750 grams okra, washed with stems trimmed

steps: Fry the sliced onion in the oil until lightly golden.
Add the meat and fry it with the onions until it changes colour.
Add 750 ml of hot water and bring to the boil. Turn the heat down and simmer gently for about 45 minutes, adding more hot water as it cooks if needed.
Add the okra, salt, pepper and tomato purée to the meat. Cook for another 10 to 15 minutes. Take care not to overcook the okra, or it turns slimy.
Add the lime juice and adjust the seasoning. Cook for another 3 to 4 minutes.
Serve with white rice.

recipes.title: Madbucha
recipes.description: A North African family recipe of tomatoes, peppers and chillies stewed down with onion and garlic, then drained and finished with tomato purée, cumin and herbs; serve cool with meat, on bread or over rice.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.note: enough to cover the bottom of the pot
or any colour, cut into small pieces
ingredient_lines.original_text: 10 bell peppers, cut into small pieces

steps: Take a pot big enough for all the ingredients, cover the bottom with oil and put it on the hob.
When the oil is hot, add the onion and garlic.
When they start to fry, add the tomatoes, peppers, chillies and salt.
Mix everything together a little and cover the pot.
Leave it to cook, stirring every so often, until the liquid comes up higher than the vegetables.
Drain off most, but not all, of the liquid.
Add the tomato purée, black pepper, cumin, parsley and oregano.
Mix, and leave to cool.

recipes.title: Persian apple dessert
recipes.description: A quick, fresh Persian dessert of apples whizzed in a blender with sugar, lemon juice and rose water until coarsely chopped, so it stays bright and crunchy.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 3 medium apples, peeled and cut up
1 tablespoon rose or orange flower water

steps: Put half the apples in a blender with the sugar, lemon juice, rose water and salt.
Cover and blend for 20 to 30 seconds, until coarsely chopped.
Add the rest of the apples and blend again until coarsely chopped.

recipes.title: Pudding with pistachios and rose water
recipes.description: Muhallebi, a silky milk pudding thickened with rice flour and cornflour, scented with rose water, set in a tin and cut into squares topped with chopped pistachios.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: ½–1 cup white granulated sugar (or to taste)
½ cup rose water or orange flower water (optional)

steps: Mix the milk and sugar in a large saucepan and bring slowly to a simmer, so the milk doesn't burn.
Make a slurry by mixing the rice flour and cornflour into the water. Stirring all the time, slowly add it to the simmering milk.
Simmer gently for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring often, until the mixture is thick enough to coat a spoon. Take it off the heat.
Stir in the rose water or orange blossom water.
Pour into a 23 × 33 cm baking tin and chill in the fridge until cold and set.
Cut into squares of about 10 cm.
Put the squares on dessert plates and scatter over the chopped pistachios.

recipes.title: Chu chee fish
recipes.description: A whole bream fried golden in a wok, then smothered in a rich chu chee curry sauce of coconut milk, fish sauce and lime leaves, finished with coriander and fresh red chilli.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

ingredient_lines.original_text: 650 g whole bream or similar fish

ingredient_lines.note: keep back 1 tbsp to fry the curry paste
ingredient_lines.original_text: 1 metric cup vegetable oil (reserve 1 tablespoon for stir-frying curry paste)
1 teaspoon of kaeng chu chee curry paste
1 tablespoon (warning: perhaps the metric 20 mL one) fish sauce

steps: Heat most of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat and fry the fish until golden on one side, about 5 minutes.
Lower the heat and carefully turn the fish over with tongs.
Turn the heat up again and cook until the second side is golden and the fish is cooked through, flaking easily at the thickest part. Lift it carefully onto a serving plate with the tongs.
Pour the oil out of the wok, then gently stir-fry the curry paste and lime leaves in the tablespoon of oil you kept back.
Add the coconut milk and fish sauce and simmer for about 5 minutes.
Add the sugar and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Taste, and add more coconut milk, fish sauce or sugar if it needs it.
Pour the sauce over the fish and garnish with the coriander and chopped chilli.

recipes.title: Mực nhồi thịt
recipes.description: Vietnamese stuffed squid: small squid filled with their chopped tentacles, pork, garlic and mushrooms, then baked in a clay pot of chicken stock, fish sauce and caramel sauce with carrot and bamboo shoots.
recipes.source: Adapted from the Wikibooks Cookbook (CC BY-SA 4.0), converted to metric, ingredients restructured

lines.note: small, cleaned, tentacles removed and kept
lines.original_text: 12 small squid, cleaned, with tentacles removed and reserved

lines.note: dried, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes and quartered
lines.original_text: 2 dried black mushrooms, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes and quartered
30 grams bamboo shoots, drained and sliced

lines.note: dried, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes, stalks removed, finely chopped
lines.original_text: 2 dried black mushrooms, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes, stems removed, and finely chopped

steps: For the stuffing, mix the chopped squid tentacles, pork and garlic.
Add the chopped spring onion and mushrooms to the squid mixture, with the fish sauce, sugar, salt and pepper.
Stuff the mixture into the squid bodies and close the openings with cocktail sticks.
Put the stuffed squid in a casserole dish or clay pot with the carrot, bamboo shoots, spring onion lengths, quartered mushrooms and their soaking liquid, caramel sauce, chicken stock and fish sauce.
Put the dish in an oven heated to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake for 20 minutes, until the stuffing is cooked through and reaches 75°C in the centre. Give it a few minutes longer if it needs it.
Serve in the pot, with steamed rice.
